# Draft:Love Is A Kingdom

Love Is a Kingdom is the third EP by Nigerian singer-songwriter Tems, released on November 21, 2025, via RCA Records and Since ’93. The surprise drop features seven tracks and marks a more intimate, introspective turn for the artist, who is credited with writing, composing, and largely producing the project herself.
Background and Release
Tems surprised fans by releasing Love Is a Kingdom without prior announcement on November 21, 2025.   The EP comes on the heels of her 2024 album Born in the Wild, which was nominated for Best Global Music Album at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards.
Composition and Themes
Musically, Love Is a Kingdom blends alt‑R&B, Afrobeats, neo-soul, and minimalist production to create a warm, deeply personal atmosphere.  Lyrically, the EP explores themes of vulnerability, love, self-worth, healing, and spiritual clarity.
The opening track, "First", is often interpreted as a declaration of self-renewal and reclaimed identity.   On “I’m Not Sure”, she reflects on uncertainty in love, while “Big Daddy” delivers a bold, witty perspective on a complicated relationship with someone who craves authority but failed to support her in the past.   In “Lagos Love,” Tems offers a soulful ode to her hometown, combining romance and a sense of rootedness.
On “Mine,” she expresses an intimate emotional surrender, and “What You Need” confronts the imbalance in love.   Finally, “Is There a Reason?” serves as a spiritually infused meditation, contemplating faith, purpose, and divine alignment.

Love Is a Kingdom was met with generally favorable reviews from critics.
RGM (Ratings Game Music) gave the EP an 86%, praising Tems’ vocal performance, her emotional range, and the way she blends vintage R&B textures with more contemporary production.
NotJustOk applauded the EP’s intimacy, noting that Tems trades the grandeur of larger productions for a “warm, minimal” sound that puts her voice at the fore.
OkayAfrica highlighted Tems’ lyrical maturity, the review emphasized how she interrogates the nature of love, self-worth, and emotional sovereignty, calling her perspective both “direct” and poetically vulnerable.
Other commentary:
Rap-Up described the production as “stripped-down,” emphasizing Tems’ use of her signature falsetto and the absence of guest features.
According to NotJustOk, the closing track feels “almost like a prayer,” suggesting a deeply introspective and spiritual layer to the EP.
In a review on GetUnruly, the reviewer described the EP as a “statement” of self-sovereignty, saying Tems “centers her own emotional sovereignty” and “commands her narrative.”
Production
Tems is credited for the majority of the writing, composing, and production, showcasing her evolving creative control.   She collaborated with a few other producers on some tracks, including GuiltyBeatz, AOD, and LONDON.
Reception
The EP has been praised for its emotional authenticity and understated production.   Critics have noted that it feels more private and meditative compared to her more expansive work , a withdrawal into a quieter, more vulnerable place.
Fans have also responded positively, calling the EP a “masterpiece” and emphasizing Tems’ songwriting and production prowess.
Visuals
Alongside the EP release, Tems dropped a visualizer for the song “Big Daddy,” directed by Jyde Ajala.   She also teased the EP earlier with a cinematic trailer featuring imagery that evokes spiritual and emotional themes, scenes include her submerged in water, looking out a window, and wearing an angelic white dress.
Track listing
Personnel
Tems – lead vocals, songwriting, production, composing
GuiltyBeatz – co-producer on selected tracks
AOD – co-producer
LONDON – co-producer
